recap.workouts:
Nothing has landed for today, and I will say that plainly rather than dress it up.

The check, so you know it was a real one and not an assumption: the 18:30 data pull found no activity of any kind dated 22 August — no ride, no run, no class — and CMI4's calendar event is still sitting on the day unpaired, at a planned load of 180. That matters, because an unpaired event alongside an actual same-sport activity is the signature of a pairing failure after an early stop, and that is not what this is. There is no activity to pair. The phone sync last wrote at 07:31 this morning with the soreness rating in and nothing else, so it has nothing to add either way.

If the ride did happen and simply has not uploaded yet, ignore all of this — tomorrow morning's pull will find it and the week reads exactly as it was written.

Worth putting next to it, because a blank Saturday is not the same thing as a blank week: week 11 stands at seven of the eight endurance sessions completed, five of five classes, and all six hypertrophy targets closed exactly on the engine numbers — Chest 7, Back 7, Side Delts 7, Rear Delts 7, Biceps 7, Triceps 10, no muscle short and none padded. Four load triggers fired in the process. The biggest endurance week of the block is very nearly in the bank.
recap.takeaways:
1) ADAPT, and this is the one decision of the evening. CMI4 classifies as SKIPPED — no activity, no done flag, event unpaired. I am not going to name a cause, because the file does not contain one and guessing at your state from an absence is exactly the move I should not make. What I do have is a rule, written into the week plan before the week started rather than invented tonight: CMI4 is the protected session, and if Saturday goes, it slides to Sunday and RF12 comes out — never watered down into a medium ride, because a diluted threshold session is full fatigue cost for no adaptation. That gate is now applied. Tomorrow is CMI4; RF12 is absorbed. It is written into WEEK_11_PLAN.md under Midweek adjustments so it is on the record and can be argued with.

2) The ninety minutes of RF12 are absorbed, not owed. Lost easy volume never gets chased, and it especially does not get bolted onto week 12, which is the deload. Nothing else in the week moves, because there is nothing else left in it.

3) One honest caveat on the slide: it puts 180 minutes with forty minutes of Zone 3 in it on the day immediately before a deload week. That is a defensible place for it — better than the middle of a build week — but it is also the reason tomorrow has a real down-branch rather than a token one. If the reason today did not happen is that you are deeper in the hole than the numbers show, that is the more useful thing to tell me tomorrow than any session is.

4) Standing item, and this is the last evening it can be settled: Sunday's plan-gen writes the week-12 deload, so the deload question has to be answered before it. The question, unchanged — how do we make a deload week actually deload, given that the gym is where the load sits? A gym cap is off the table, decided 1 August, and I am not re-proposing it. The numbers half is repaired and ready: deduplicated, week 10 ran 10.8% raw and 11.9% corrected above week 9, an ordinary build-week step just over your own 1.05–1.10 rule, on a week that cleared 80/20 at 81.4% easy with three hard stimuli. So this starts from a measured ramp and a clean distribution, not a crisis. The lever is yours to pick.
recap.tomorrow:
CMI4 moves to Sunday and RF12 comes out — the plan's own gate, not a new decision. 180 minutes: 20′ Zone 1, then 2 × (20′ Zone 3 at 222–248 W / 15′ Zone 1), then 10 × (1′ Zone 4 at 248–283 W / 2′ Zone 1), then 60′ Zone 1. Target 222–235 W on block one, set the effort in the first five minutes and then stop negotiating with it. The interval content is identical to CMI1 and CMI2, both of which you have already ridden; the only new thing is the hour of Zone 1 at the end, and that hour is the session rather than a cool-down. Fuel it like the three-hour ride it is. No gym, no lifting.

Signals to read: whether 222 W in the opening five minutes feels like a number you are holding or one that is holding you; where heart rate settles in block one against 159; and in the Zone 4 set, whether you can get back to Zone 1 watts inside the full two-minute recovery.

Legs willing and heart rate plateauing clearly under 159 in block one? Ride it exactly as written — block two a touch firmer if it is there, all ten Zone 4 reps, and the full sixty-minute tail. Legs heavy, or it is the tail specifically that is in doubt? Ride the intervals as written and shorten the tail — that is the plan's own gate and it is the right way round, because you never trade the tail for firmer intervals. The on-bike gate stands either way: if rep power falls under 248 W or you cannot get back to Zone 1 inside the 2′, stop the set and spin out the rest. Both are a good day's work.

And if today's ride did happen and simply has not uploaded, then nothing moves: Sunday is RF12 as written — 5′ Zone 1, 80′ Zone 2 at 5:01–5:45/km, 5′ Zone 1, governed off a heart-rate ceiling of 145 the way you ran it last week.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.
recapPrev.tomorrow:
CAn4 — 90' on the bike: 10' Z1, then 6 × (2:30 Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 5:00 Z1), 30' Zone 2 @ 165–196 W, 5' Z1. Both bands are the post-CT31 numbers (FTP 236 W). No gym, no class — Saturday is bike only.

Sunday is full rest either way. That part isn't negotiable.

recovery.bannerTitle: WEEK 12 SEEDED — the deload, and the block's two threshold retests
recovery.bannerSub: Five endurance sessions, 6:30 total, down 35.6% on week 11. CT31 on Wednesday and RT19 on Sunday set every zone number for weeks 13–21. Monday's morning run replaces this banner with a real reading.
recovery.note: Week 12 is seeded and the shape of it is simple: two retests, and everything else arranged to protect them. CT31 (Wed, 24′ Zone 3) and RT19 (Sun, 20′ Zone 3) are the block-boundary retest, they are analysed automatically by the evening recap, and their output writes zones.json — which means they set the bands every session in weeks 13 to 21 gets prescribed from. A retest run on wrecked legs does not read as tired, it reads as threshold down, and then nine weeks get prescribed too easy. That is why Friday's Captain Redbeard gets scaled to step-overs and the lighter ball, and why the long ride and the run retest are the way round they are: CFF16 on Saturday buys RT19 a second day of separation from 100 box jump overs, and a steady ride does far less muscle damage the day before a run test than a metcon does. Endurance drops from 10:06 across 8 sessions to 6:30 across 5. Hypertrophy drops from 45 upper sets to 25, generated by progression.py --week 12 and checked back against the engine. Six load bumps earned in week 11 are BANKED to week 13 rather than applied — the full list is in WEEK_12_PLAN.md so nothing gets lost. One thing to know before you read any analysis numbers this week: all six analysis-cache modules were refused on staleness tonight. They were generated at 05:57 and plan-gen ran at 16:11, past the 8-hour threshold, so no polarization figure, no fatigue level, no load figure and no progress count appear anywhere in this week's plan. That is a refusal rather than a gap papered over. The cause, corrected after you flagged it: the schedule has NOT drifted — plan-gen is 18:03 Sunday and the refresh is 17:45, which works. This run was started manually at 16:11, before the refresh, so it read the morning cache. The real gap is that any off-schedule run loses all six modules with no way to recover inside the run.

end.name: CF3 — 30′ easy · carries the 165 W reference block
end.detail: The shortest ride on the calendar to date, and it carries the week's most important measurement. 10 of the 20 Zone 2 minutes are held at a fixed 165 W, placed at minutes 5–15
end.desc:
5′ Zone 1 @ 118–165 W → 20′ Zone 2 @ 165–196 W → 5′ Zone 1. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 23 Aug — CF3 is 30 minutes, the shortest CF-family ride used in the block.)
This ride carries the 10′ @ 165 W reference block. It replaces ten of the twenty Zone 2 minutes rather than adding to them, so the session is still 30 minutes. Placed at minutes 5–15, early in the ride and deliberately so. Regenerate with python make_zwo.py CF3 --ref-block — it pins the FTP override so Zwift's stored number cannot shift the target.
165 W is a fixed wattage, not a zone. It does not move on Wednesday when CT31 retunes FTP, and that is the entire point: it is the only repeated measure the progress track has. Hold it flat and let heart rate say whatever it says.
Why CF3 and not Saturday's much longer CFF16. This measurement is only worth anything as a repeated one, and every prior observation sits early in the Zone 2 block of a short CF-family ride. Dropping this week's block into minute 100 of a 150-minute ride would add an hour and a half of drift to one observation and nothing to the others — a bigger confound than the block exists to remove. If CF3 gets cut, the block moves to CFF16 at minutes 10–20, not later.
One confound to declare: if CMI4 was in fact ridden on Sunday, today's block carries that fatigue and the observation should be annotated rather than discarded. That is what the confound field is for.

end.name: CT31 — 60′ · BIKE THRESHOLD RETEST
end.detail: The block-boundary retest. tune.py analyses this automatically tonight and writes zones.json — it sets FTP and bike LTHR for weeks 13 to 21
end.desc:
5′ Zone 1 → 15′ Zone 2 @ 165–196 W → 24′ Zone 3 tune block @ 222–248 W → 11′ Zone 2 → 5′ Zone 1. (Verified library structure.)
This is the same session that set FTP 236 on 28 July, so the comparison is direct and like-for-like.
Set the effort in the first 3–4 minutes and then stop adjusting. One early correction, never a stair-step. tune.py reads steadiness as a coefficient of variation, and a sawtooth block reads as a dirty measurement even when the average is right.
Target the band and let heart rate tell the story. Last time the block averaged 229.5 W with the plateau at 158.5 against a bike LTHR of 159 — that is what a clean one looks like.
Do not ride it as a test of how much you can hurt. A block you fade out of measures your pacing, not your threshold. If heart rate is clearly under 159 at 24 minutes you have left something on the table — and that is the better of the two errors.
If today arrives genuinely flat, MOVE the retest to Thursday and drop RAn3. Do not water it down. A half-executed tune block costs full fatigue, produces a number anyway, and that number then sets nine weeks of zones.

cf.name: Captain Redbeard (time) — THE WEEK'S NON-NEGOTIABLE SCALE. [FITNESS], and step-overs all five rounds

For time — descending row ladder, each row followed by 20 wall balls 20/14 and 20 box jump overs: 1000/900 m · 800/700 m · 600/500 m · 400/300 m · 200/150 m. [FITNESS]: 900/800 m start, wall balls 16/12.

Box jump OVERS are the expensive part. The landing is the eccentric cost, and step-overs remove nearly all of it for almost no loss of stimulus. If one thing in this week gets scaled, it is this, and it is worth more than any other adjustment available.
Row it steady and stop caring about the clock. Sunday's RT19 sets the run anchors for the whole Race-Specific block; there is no version of Friday that is worth more than that.

end.name: CFF16 — 150′ Zone 2 with a 15′ Zone 3 fast finish
end.detail: The week's aerobic ballast and the reason the week still clears 81% easy while carrying two retests. The Zone 3 is at the END and there is no cool-down segment
end.desc:
5′ Zone 1 → 130′ Zone 2 @ 165–196 W → 15′ Zone 3 @ 222–248 W (fast finish). (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 23 Aug — CFF = fast finish. Do not read the 16 as short: CFF16 is 150 minutes, and the Zone 3 sits at the end with no cool-down listed.)
The 130 minutes are the session; the 15 are the seasoning.
Ride the Zone 2 in the band — 196 W is the ceiling and Zone X starts one watt later. On a ride this long the drift upward is unconscious rather than decided, which is exactly what makes it dangerous to the week's ratio.
The fast finish is 15 minutes at 222–248 W on two-hour legs, which is a genuinely different and more useful skill than the same fifteen minutes fresh. If the Zone 2 body was ridden too firm, do the finish anyway at the bottom of Zone 3 — do not compensate by making it harder.
Yes, this is a deload week and yes, this is a 150-minute ride. Both are true. It is the grid's own prescription for the row and the week's hours still fall 35.6%. Long easy volume is what a deload protects, not what it cuts.
If you are flat, ride the 130′ Zone 2 and skip the finish. Keep the volume, drop the intensity — never the reverse. That is the week's second cut, behind RAn3.
Why the weekend is this way round: this ride sits between Friday's metcon and Sunday's retest on purpose, because a steady ride does far less muscle damage the day before a run test than 100 box jump overs would.

end.name: RT19 — 90′ · RUN THRESHOLD RETEST
end.detail: The session that establishes the run anchors for the Race-Specific phase. tune.py analyses it automatically tonight and writes zones.json
end.desc:
5′ Zone 1 → 10′ Zone 2 @ 5:01–5:45/km → 20′ Zone 3 tune block @ 4:22–4:42/km → 50′ Zone 2 → 5′ Zone 1. (Verified library structure.)
Same code that measured your run anchors on 30 July, when 19.6 minutes at 4:27/km produced a heart-rate plateau of 167 with only +4.0 bpm of drift — the clean read that finally replaced the placeholder 162 copied off the bike.
Two things to get right. First, the 20′ block is threshold, not a time trial. 4:27/km is the reference and the band is 4:22–4:42. You said last time you could have held it about an hour — that is exactly the right feeling. Second, the 50 minutes afterwards must actually be Zone 2. Finishing the block and never coming back down is the classic error in this session and it is what turns a 90-minute run into an hour of Zone X.
Terrain note, settled 30 July: if you run this outdoors on rolling ground, the pace and heart-rate scatter that produces is terrain, not an execution fault — tune.py reads steadiness on a 30-second smoothed basis for exactly this reason. Run the effort, not the watch.
The honest caveat: this follows a 150-minute ride. If the block reads soft, that is a live alternative explanation to threshold down and it should be weighed before any anchor moves.
If today arrives genuinely flat, MOVE it into Monday of week 13 rather than watering it down. And per mandate §3 — deep soreness plus subjective slog on the Sunday of a deload week is your documented signature that the deload did not work. If today feels like that, that is information about the deload, not about your threshold, and it is a reason to move the retest rather than accept a low number.
